chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When Adam (peace be upon him) died, the prayer over him was reported. Hibatullah said to Jibril (peace be upon him), 'Advance, O Messenger of Allah, and pray over the Prophet of Allah.' Jibril (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, Allah commanded us to prostrate for your father, so we do not advance ahead of the most righteous of his offspring, and you are among the most righteous of them.' So he advanced and said Takbir five times, the number of the prayer that Allah prescribed upon the nation of Muhammad, and it is the Sunnah that continues among his offspring until the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.آدَمُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Adam (peace be upon him), the first human and prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the origin and number of Takbirs in the prayer over the dead according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the Sunnah of Salat al-Mayyit by linking the five Takbirs performed by Jibril over Adam to the prayer prescribed for the Ummah of Muhammad, thereby grounding the ritual in primordial tradition. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the hierarchy of righteousness, where Jibril defers to Adam as the most righteous of his offspring, illustrating the continuity of divine honor across prophetic lineages. This event serves as a foundational proof for the specific number of Takbirs in the funeral prayer, a point of discussion among jurists regarding its status as a confirmed Sunnah versus a mandatory act.
